details: The first line is followed by a blank line, the source line as "N| code", a caret line under the reported token or expression (one pair per line for an expression over several lines), and zero or more "Hint: ..." lines. A long type mismatch adds "It is:" and "It needs:" lines. A run reports every error of a phase (parsing, name resolution, type checking; one per top-level declaration), in source order with a blank line between them, at most 20 then "... and N more", followed by a count such as "3 errors" when there are several. The report ends with a line such as "For more on ELCI2005, run `elci explain ELCI2005`.". Configuration and command-line errors are printed as "elci: ELCI4001: message".

report.output: JSON Lines on standard error: one JSON object per error, one per line; one error is one line

explain.output: the long-form entry for a code (ELCI2002, elci2002 or 2002): meaning, causes, a failing example, the fix
explain.list: elci explain with no code lists every code with its title

color: --color=auto|always|never; auto colours a terminal unless NO_COLOR is set; JSON is never coloured

codes.meaning: Invalid source character or literal
Malformed or unsupported syntax
Invalid pattern or expression form, including a constructor pattern with the wrong number of arguments and a record pattern on a library record
Type mismatch, or a type that would have to contain itself
Unsupported equality, ordering or append type; a constrained type variable (`comparable`, `appendable`) missing or misnamed, or `number`; a `Dict` decoded from Data whose keys are not comparable
Missing required top-level signature
Unknown value name
Duplicate binder or unreachable pattern
Non-exhaustive case expression
Eager recursive value cycle
Non-concrete handler or entrypoint
Unknown or unconstrained record field
Duplicate type or constructor, or a built-in constructor or type name (`Just`, `Nothing`, `True`, `False`; `Int`, `Maybe`, `List` and the other built-in types)
Invalid type, alias, arity or alias cycle; `Tuple` or `Unit` written as a type name
Unsupported serialized boundary type (including a `Value`, which has no strict boundary codec yet), or a value without a Data encoding (a function or an `Array`) stored in data
Validator handler signature does not match its configured purpose, parameters or datum profile
Unknown or missing module or imported export; a source module importing the test library
Ambiguous name: two imports, possibly a default import, expose different things under it
Entrypoint or handler is not exposed by its module

Source module path, ownership or cycle error; reserved core module name or alias; qualified reference to an unexposed or unimported name, a name a core module lacks or an Elm function Elci does not provide

Unsupported Java export signature, with provider reason; a Java export whose result can hold the ledger `Value` (except Julc's `ContextsLib` and `OutputLib`), which Java libraries do not keep canonical
PIR lowering cannot represent the inferred program, such as `Julc.Data.decode` or a generic Java export at a type nothing determines
Specialization or polymorphic-recursion limit

Generic library type argument violates the export's constraint (for example `DATA_ENCODABLE`), or contains a `Dict` or a `Value`, which a Java library could build without the key-order or canonical-form check; a `Julc.Data` conversion of a type without a Data encoding, such as a function

Invalid project configuration or CLI request (`elci.toml`, `elci init`, options, `elci explain`), including a `[java-modules]` key that names a core module, an `elci apply` parameter that doesn't fit its type (such as a `Dict` whose keys are not strictly ascending) and a source file that is not UTF-8
Julc backend rejected generated PIR; reported at the Elci declaration it names, with the `JULC00xx` code
The Julc backend lacks a contract revision or capability the program needs
